data.gender_notes: Maxwell is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Maxwell is derived from the Latin name Maximus, which means 'greatest' or 'largest'. This name was given to emperors and powerful warriors in ancient Rome. The name Maxwell was popularized in Scotland during the Middle Ages due to the influence of the Roman empire. The name Maxwell carries the meaning “Great warrior” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Latin. Parents who choose Maxwell usually hope their child will grow to embody great warrior and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: Maxwell was a Anglicized version of the Scottish name Maccolm or Macquhalium, which translates to 'son of the greatest hero'. The name became popular in England during the Middle Ages and was also used for persons of significant power and authority, such as nobles and clergymen. In modern times, Maxwell has been associated with successful and influential figures such as James Clerk Maxwell, a renowned physicist, Mathew Maxwell and Tim Maxwell, prominent sports personalities, and Maxwell Perkins, a distinguished literary agent.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Maxwell holds spiritual significance as it imparts a sense of strength and courage. It is a reminder that every individual possesses the potential to rise above challenges and achieve greatness. Maxwell can be seen as a name that symbolizes the divine gift of power and the potential to make a meaningful impact on the world. It is a name that inspires individuals to live their lives with purpose and to pursue their aspirations with determination and resilience. The name Maxwell can also be seen as a reminder of the ultimate power and greatness of God, who is the source of all strength and ability.
